beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Foundations and Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. Topics include the knowledge discovery process; data exploration and its role; data extraction, cleaning, integration and transformation; handling numeric, unstructured, text, web, and other forms of data; and ethical issues underlying data preparation and mining. Consider this worked case: Students will review the official course catalog to confirm that data cleaning projects and a paper are required for credit. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Course Foundations and Scope
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display the official course catalog excerpt highlighting the knowledge discovery process and required deliverables.

beats.narration: Now define Data Exploration and Its Role precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Data cleaning projects and a paper are required. Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate how exploratory data analysis reveals missing values and outliers in a sample dataset. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Data Exploration and Its Role
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a split-screen comparison of raw data versus explored data highlighting identified anomalies.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Data Extraction and Cleaning operates in a concrete sequence. Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules. Consider this worked case: Students will practice extracting structured data from a CSV file and removing duplicate rows using standard cleaning techniques. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Data Extraction and Cleaning
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Animate the step-by-step removal of duplicate rows and standardization of date formats in a spreadsheet.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Data Integration and Transformation and make the decision criteria explicit. Queries select, join, aggregate, insert, update, and delete data. Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate merging two relational tables and converting categorical variables into numeric codes. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis. Then summarize what the example demonstrates, what it does not establish, and what evidence would be needed next.
beats.title: Data Integration and Transformation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a before-and-after table showing merged columns and transformed categorical values.

beats.narration: Apply Handling Numeric Data to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. This course provides an introduction to the concepts and techniques used in preparing data for subsequent data mining. Consider this worked case: Students will calculate the mean and median to impute missing numeric values and apply min-max normalization to a dataset. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Handling Numeric Data
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a bar chart comparing raw numeric values versus normalized values ranging from 0 to 1.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Handling Unstructured and Text Data, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Constraints and indexes support data integrity and efficient lookup. Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate converting a paragraph of text into a list of tokens and removing common stop words. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Handling Unstructured and Text Data
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a word cloud transitioning from raw text to a cleaned token list with stop words highlighted.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Handling Web Data with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types. Consider this worked case: Students will scrape a static webpage, parse the HTML structure, and extract structured records while respecting server rate limits. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Handling Web Data
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a flowchart of the web scraping process from request to parsed JSON output.

beats.narration: Use Data Integrity and Constraints to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries. Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate how primary keys and foreign keys prevent duplicate and orphaned records in a relational database. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Data Integrity and Constraints
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a database schema diagram highlighting primary key and foreign key relationships.

beats.narration: Connect Ethical Issues in Data Preparation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Nodes and relationships can carry properties. Consider this worked case: Students will review a case study on anonymizing personal data and ensuring fair representation in cleaned datasets. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Ethical Issues in Data Preparation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a checklist of ethical guidelines for data preparation and mining.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Labels group nodes that play a similar domain role. Consider this worked case: Students will complete a checklist verifying extraction accuracy, cleaning completeness, transformation consistency, and ethical compliance. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a printable checklist template with checkboxes for each verification step.

Topics include the knowledge discovery process; data exploration and its role; data extraction, cleaning, integration and transformation; handling numeric, unstructured, text, web, and other forms of data; and ethical issues underlying data preparation and mining. sources.author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
sources.excerpt: Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types. Primary keys identify rows, while foreign keys express references between tables. Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules. Queries select, join, aggregate, insert, update, and delete data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries. Transactions group operations into an atomic unit of work. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another. Schema design separates entities and relationships, while normalization addresses update anomalies. Query planning and physical structures influence performance without changing logical query meaning.
sources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation

sources.author: Neo4j
sources.excerpt: Property graph models represent domain entities as nodes. Relationships connect nodes and have a type and direction. Nodes and relationships can carry properties. Labels group nodes that play a similar domain role. A useful graph model begins from the questions the application must answer. Traversal patterns determine which relationships the application follows. Identity must be explicit when several records may describe the same entity. Constraints and indexes support data integrity and efficient lookup. Direction, cardinality, and update behavior are part of the model.
sources.title: Neo4j Graph Data Modeling
